question.text: A portfolio manager running a global fixed-income portfolio hedges USD bond holdings into INR. According to the workbook, the typical derivative used to hedge such currency exposures is a:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook identifies currency risk as a feature of global fixed-income investments and notes that portfolio managers use currency swaps to hedge such exposures. A currency swap is defined as an exchange of payments in two different currencies, including (typically) an exchange of notional principal at the start and end of the contract, which makes it well-suited to hedging the cash flows on a USD-denominated bond back to INR. The Trap: An Interest Rate Swap hedges rate risk, not currency risk. A Credit Default Swap hedges credit risk. Equity futures are unrelated to bond currency hedging. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), pp. 348-350.
